userStories.title: Forge: commenter access, comment author id, item comments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose commenter write-access checks, GitLab author ids and resolvable item comments through @/forge.

**Motivation** — Those rulings live in a git-ignored sidecar (`src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts`) next to the run, so a fresh checkout (a `nax bot` checkout, a koda job) cannot see them, and nobody can rule from the PR.

**Approach** — `PrComment` (`src/forge/pr-types.ts`). Baseline: `{ id, kind, author, body, createdAt }`. Target: adds `readonly authorId?: number`, set from the GitLab note's `author.id` (`GitlabDiscussion.notes[].author` gains `id: number`) and left unset on GitHub.

`hasWriteAccess` (`src/forge/trust.ts`, private). Baseline: `(ref, info: PrInfo, deps, cwd)`. Target: an exported `hasWriteAccess(ref, who: { login: string; id?: number }, deps, cwd): Promise<boolean>` in a new `src/forge/access.ts`; the private helpers `readError`, `parseReply` and `api` move to a new leaf `src/forge/api-reply.ts` that both `trust.ts` and `access.ts` import (no cycle); `classifyPrTrust` calls `hasWriteAccess(ref, info.author, ...)`, behaviour unchanged.

`src/forge/comments.ts`. Target: adds `postItemComment(ref, { path, body, headSha }, deps, cwd): Promise<PostedComment>`: on GitHub a file-level review comment (`subject_type=file`, `path`, `commit_id`, no line); on GitLab a discussion with no position (a resolvable general thread). Exported from `@/forge`.

**Scope** — In: the two new forge leaves, trust rewiring, authorId mappings, postItemComment, public exports, access/item-write tests and GitLab note fixtures. Out: item formatting/posting (US-002/005), collaborator ruling state and recording (US-004/009), readiness (US-012).

**Interface** — `hasWriteAccess(ref, who: { login: string; id?: number }, deps, cwd): Promise<boolean>`; `postItemComment(ref, { path, body, headSha }, deps, cwd): Promise<PostedComment>`; `readonly authorId?: number`. Preserve GitHub write/admin and GitLab >=30 semantics, explicit host arguments, NaxError failures and pre-write MAX_FORGE_COMMENT_CHARS validation.

Regression edits: `test/unit/forge/threads.test.ts` — GitLab thread comments are compared with deep equality on `{ id, kind, author, body, createdAt }`; they now also carry `authorId` from the note author's `id`. The invariant: every other field is unchanged and GitHub comments carry no `authorId`. `test/unit/forge/threads-comments.test.ts` — GitLab note fixtures and expectations gain the author `id` and `authorId`; the invariant: ordering and every other field are unchanged.

userStories.title: Item thread formats
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add pure durable item identities and opener, echo, ask, closed and index formats for workflow PR comments.

**Motivation** — Those rulings live in a git-ignored sidecar (`src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts`) next to the run, so a fresh checkout (a `nax bot` checkout, a koda job) cannot see them, and nobody can rule from the PR.

**Approach** — All keys go through `withNaxBotMarker` / `parseNaxBotMarker` (`src/forge/marker.ts`), key grammar `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}`.

- **Item key:** `w-<itemId>.<h8>`, where `<h8>` is the first 8 hex characters of SHA-256 over `<kind>\n<issue>` of the `OpenItem`. Positional ids such as `_run:cv1` therefore get a new key when their text changes.
- **Postable item:** its id matches `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` and the longest derived key, `wq-<itemKey>-` followed by 20 characters, is at most 128 characters. An item that is not postable is skipped (logged); its key is still written to the index, so readiness holds the PR (fail closed).
- **Item thread opener** (body passed to `withNaxBotMarker` with the item key): first line `Open item **<itemId>** (<kind>): <issue>`, `<issue>` through `safeInline`; then `Suggestion: <suggestion>` when the item has one and `Advisor: <action> — <why>` when it has a ruling (both through `safeInline`); then the line `Rule on it by replying: fixed <sha>, waive: <reason>, confirm, override: <reason>, or verified. Any other reply from a collaborator is read as a ruling only when its meaning is clear.`
- **Ruling echo key:** `wr-<disposition>-<itemKey>`, `<disposition>` one of the sidecar `DISPOSITIONS` (`fixed`, `waived`, `confirmed`, `overridden`, `verified`), none of which contains `-`.
- **Ruling echo body:** first line `Recorded: <disposition> — <reason>` (or `Recorded: fixed in <sha7> — <reason>`), reason through `safeInline`; second line `By @<login>`, or `By nax bot` for a bot ruling; third line `To change it, reply on this thread.`
- **Ask key:** `wq-<itemKey>-<replyId>`; body `I could not read a ruling from that reply. Start a reply with fixed <sha>, waive: <reason>, confirm, override: <reason> or verified.`
- **Closed key:** `wc-<itemKey>`; body `No longer open in the run at <sha7>.` (not a ruling).
- **Index comment:** a top-level PR comment with key `w-index`; body lines `nax workflow open items: <n>`, `Reviewed head: <40-hex sha>` or `Reviewed head: none`, `Reviewed base: <40-hex sha>` (the run's seed; written only with a reviewed head), then one line per item key in `buildOpenItems` order, each `- <itemKey>`.
- **Evidence comment:** `evidenceComment(entries)` wrapped with key `w-evidence`; edited in place when it exists.

`src/workflow/item-threads.ts` (pure formats; imports only `node:crypto`, `./pr-body-safe`, `@/forge` and types, never `./pr-body`, which reaches `@/finish` and from there `@/cli`).

**Scope** — In: keys/postability, opener/echo/ask/index render/parse and shared PrRuling/ItemIndex types. Out: keyword parsing (US-003), thread state (US-004), forge posting/index closing (US-005/006), evidence writes (US-012). Do not introduce a dependency on US-003's future file in this independent story.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface PrRuling {
  readonly itemKey: string;
  readonly itemId: string;
  readonly disposition: Disposition;
  readonly reason: string;            // one line, non-empty
  readonly sha?: string;              // required when disposition is "fixed"
  readonly by: string | null;         // login; null = nax bot
}
export interface ItemIndex { readonly reviewedHead?: string; readonly reviewedBase?: string; readonly keys: readonly string[] }
```
`itemKey(item)`, `isPostable(item)`, `renderItemOpener(item)`, `parseItemOpener(body)`, `renderRulingEcho(ruling)`, `parseRulingEcho(key, body)`, `askKey(itemKey, replyId)`, `renderRulingAsk()`, `renderItemIndex(index)`, `parseItemIndex(body)`.

[unit] itemKey({ id: "_run:cv1", kind: "cannot-verify", issue: "x" }) returns w-_run:cv1. followed by the first 8 hex characters of SHA-256 over cannot-verify
x.
[unit] itemKey of two items with the same id and different issue text returns different keys.

[unit] parseItemOpener of a renderItemOpener body returns the item's id and kind.
[unit] renderRulingEcho of a waived ruling with reason ok by alice returns the lines Recorded: waived — ok, By @alice, To change it, reply on this thread.

userStories.title: Ruling keyword grammar
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse deterministic collaborator ruling keywords from the first non-empty reply line.

**Motivation** — Those rulings live in a git-ignored sidecar (`src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts`) next to the run, so a fresh checkout (a `nax bot` checkout, a koda job) cannot see them, and nobody can rule from the PR.

**Approach** — Keyword grammar (`parseRulingKeyword`), applied to the reply's first non-empty line after trimming, case-insensitive on the keyword:

| First line | Ruling |
|---|---|
| `fixed <sha>` (`<sha>` 7-40 hex), optional ` — <reason>`, ` - <reason>` or `: <reason>` | `fixed`, sha, reason (default `fixed`) |
| `waive: <reason>` / `waived: <reason>` | `waived`, reason (non-empty required) |
| `confirm` / `confirmed`, optional `: <reason>` | `confirmed`, reason (default `confirmed`) |
| `override: <reason>` / `overridden: <reason>` | `overridden`, reason (non-empty required) |
| `verified` / `verify`, optional `: <reason>` | `verified`, reason (default `verified`) |
| anything else, or `waive`/`override` with an empty reason | not a keyword ruling (`null`) |

**Scope** — In: pure src/workflow/ruling-keyword.ts and table-driven grammar tests. Out: comment formats (US-002), access checks/recording (US-009), model fallback (US-008/010).

**Interface** — `parseRulingKeyword(text)` in `src/workflow/ruling-keyword.ts` (pure), using the sidecar `Disposition` vocabulary. Return the disposition, one-line reason and optional fixed sha, or null; do not infer rulings from conversational text.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] parseRulingKeyword("waive: flaky upstream") returns { disposition: "waived", reason: "flaky upstream" }.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("WAIVE:   ") returns null.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("fixed abc1234 — moved the guard") returns { disposition: "fixed", sha: "abc1234", reason: "moved the guard" }.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("fixed abc1234") returns a fixed ruling with reason fixed.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("fixed") returns null.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("Confirm") returns { disposition: "confirmed", reason: "confirmed" }.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("override: product decided") returns { disposition: "overridden", reason: "product decided" }.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("override:") returns null.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("verified: ran the smoke suite") returns { disposition: "verified", reason: "ran the smoke suite" }.

[unit] parseRulingKeyword("

  confirm
more text") reads only the first non-empty line and returns a confirmed ruling.
[unit] parseRulingKeyword("I think this is fine") returns null.

routing.reasoning: One pure grammar implementation with explicit keyword alternatives and no identity or authorization decision.

userStories.title: Post item threads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Post one owned resolvable thread per open non-CI workflow item, with location/file/anchor fallbacks.

**Motivation** — Those rulings live in a git-ignored sidecar (`src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts`) next to the run, so a fresh checkout (a `nax bot` checkout, a koda job) cannot see them, and nobody can rule from the PR.

**Approach** — `postItemThreads(input, deps)` (deps default `_featureDeps.forge`) in order:

1. `prNumberFromUrl(url)`, `resolvePrRef`, `readPrInfo`, `readCurrentUser`, `listReviewThreads`, `listPrComments`, then `readItemThreads`.
2. `items = buildOpenItems(record)` minus kind `ci`.
3. Each postable item with no own thread for its key is posted, in item order:
   - with `file` and `line`: `postInlineComment` at that location with `info.headSha` and `info.diffRefs`; on failure, `postItemComment` on `file`; on a second failure, `postItemComment` on the anchor path;
   - otherwise: `postItemComment` on the anchor path, which is `.nax/features/<feature>/prd.json` when that repo-relative path is in `changedFiles`, else the first entry of `changedFiles`; with no changed files on GitHub the item is counted in `failed` (GitLab needs no path).
6. Every forge call is wrapped: a failure is logged with the item id and the loop continues through the specified fallbacks. An item whose allowed posting attempts all fail is counted in `failed`; an initial read failure in step 1 posts nothing and returns `failed: 1`.

Posted bodies are `withNaxBotMarker(renderItemOpener(item), itemKey(item))`. An item that is not postable is skipped (logged); its key is still written to the index, so readiness holds the PR (fail closed). This story supplies the posting/failure part; US-006 adds index/closing steps 4-5. Count an ultimately unposted item as failed after exhausting its allowed fallbacks, and continue with the next item.

**Scope** — In: new item-threads-post.ts, ordered reads/selection/dedup/posting, anchor selection and failure isolation. Out: index/closing and graph wiring (US-006), reading rulings (US-009/010).

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface ItemThreadsInput {
  readonly record: WorkflowFeatureRecord; readonly url: string; readonly head?: string;
  readonly projectDir: string; readonly feature: string;
  readonly changedFiles: readonly string[];  // repo-relative, seed..head
}
export interface ItemThreadsOutcome { readonly posted: number; readonly closed: number; readonly skipped: number; readonly failed: number }
```
`postItemThreads(input, deps)` uses the shared formats/state and @/forge APIs in projectDir; closed remains zero until US-006.

userStories.title: Item index, closing, and the publish wiring
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Maintain the durable item index and obsolete-thread closures and invoke posting through an optional publish step.

**Motivation** — Those rulings live in a git-ignored sidecar (`src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts`) next to the run, so a fresh checkout (a `nax bot` checkout, a koda job) cannot see them, and nobody can rule from the PR.

**Approach** — After every `pr`-mode publish that returns a PR URL (draft or ready), the feature graph's `publish` step calls a new optional step `steps.postItemThreads` through a small new module, so `feature-steps.ts` grows by about two lines. It opens one nax bot thread per open item (`buildOpenItems` of the record, minus the `ci` item), writes or edits one nax bot index comment (current item keys plus the reviewed head), and closes earlier item threads whose key is no longer in the index. The step is optional on `FeatureSteps` (like `readCiFailures`), so the G0 equivalence goldens, which do not supply it, are unchanged.

`postItemThreadsAfterPublish(env, rec, out, head)` calls `env.steps.postItemThreads` when it is defined, `out.url` is set and `out.outcome` is `draft` or `ready`, with the record patched by this publish (outcome, ci, ciDetail, reasons, approval, storyStates), `head`, and `changedFiles` from `env.steps.changedFiles(rec.seed)` (empty when the seed is empty or the call throws). A throw from the step is logged and swallowed.

4. The index comment is written: `renderItemIndex({ keys: every item's key, reviewedHead })`, edited in place when an own `w-index` comment exists, posted otherwise. `reviewedHead` is `head` when `record.reviewRan === true` and none of `reviewUnread`, `costLimited`, `reReviewSkipped`, `gateRepairRounds > 0`, `ciRepairRounds > 0` holds; when only `ciRepairRounds > 0` fails the test, the existing index's reviewed head (and base) is kept; otherwise `none`. `Reviewed base` is `record.seed`.
5. Each own item thread whose key is not in the new index and has no own `wc-` reply gets the closed reply and is resolved. This is not a ruling.
6. Every forge call is wrapped: a failure is logged with the item id, counted in `failed`, and the loop continues. A failure in step 1 posts nothing and returns `failed: 1`.

Index comment: a top-level PR comment with key `w-index`; body lines `nax workflow open items: <n>`, `Reviewed head: <40-hex sha>` or `Reviewed head: none`, `Reviewed base: <40-hex sha>` (the run's seed; written only with a reviewed head), then one line per item key in `buildOpenItems` order, each `- <itemKey>`. Include non-postable and failed-post keys. Closed key: `wc-<itemKey>`; body `No longer open in the run at <sha7>.` (not a ruling). Own means current login AND valid marker.

**Scope** — In: extend item-threads-post.ts with index/closing, add publish-item-threads.ts, optional FeatureSteps entry, one publishStep call after publish/readHeadSoft and buildFeatureEnv real wiring. Out: item posting mechanics (US-005), bot interpretation/readiness (US-009..012), incremental range selection (US-013). Do not change the publish return patch or graph equivalence when the step is absent.

**Interface** — `postItemThreads?: (input: ItemThreadsInput) => Promise<ItemThreadsOutcome>` on `FeatureSteps`; `postItemThreadsAfterPublish(env, rec, out, head)` in `src/workflow/publish-item-threads.ts`. `publishStep`: after `env.steps.publish(rec)` and `readHeadSoft`, one call to `postItemThreadsAfterPublish(env, rec, out, head)` from the new module; the returned patch is unchanged. `buildFeatureEnv` wires the step with `_featureDeps.forge` in `fc.projectDir`. The current FeatureEnv does not expose projectDir or feature: explicitly thread the run identity captured from fc so the helper can construct ItemThreadsInput, without deriving either field from process.cwd() or making new metadata mandatory in G0 environments.

userStories.title: One CI run for an approved workflow PR
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Remove the post-approval ledger push so promotion uses CI on the unchanged published head.

**Motivation** — nax#2629: `prMode` (`src/workflow/finalize.ts`) commits and pushes the advisor's `finish-approval` ledger line after the CI wait (`pushLedger`), which starts a second full CI run and leaves the promoted PR's head pending.

**Approach** — `prMode` (`src/workflow/finalize.ts`). Baseline: calls `pushLedger(fc)` after an approval. Target: no post-approval ledger commit or push; `pushLedger` is deleted.

**Scope** — In: delete pushLedger/call and any now-unused imports/comments, preserving the pre-CI ledger commit, push, CI wait, approval and final PR update. Out: posting/index wiring (US-006), bot readiness (US-012). The `finish-approval` ledger line is no longer pushed after approval; it stays in the working tree until a later run's ledger commit, so the branch of an approved PR lacks that one line.

**Interface** — Existing `publish(fc: FeatureContext, input: PublishInput): Promise<PublishOutcome>` stays unchanged; remove the private `pushLedger(fc)` helper.

Regression edit: `test/unit/workflow/finalize.test.ts` — the test asserting a second `commitAndPush` after the approval ("Ledger push failed" warning) and any call-order expectation that includes a post-approval `ledger`/`push` pair are removed or replaced: after an approval there is no further `commitLedger` or `commitAndPush` call. The invariant: the pre-CI ledger commit and push are unchanged. New tests go in the new approval-push test file this story creates; this file must not grow (it is at 797 of 800 lines).

userStories.title: Record model-read rulings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend ruling recording with one bounded batched model read of non-keyword writer replies and idempotent clarification asks.

**Motivation** — Those rulings live in a git-ignored sidecar (`src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts`) next to the run, so a fresh checkout (a `nax bot` checkout, a koda job) cannot see them, and nobody can rule from the PR.

**Approach** — Step 4 of `recordPrRulings(input)`:

Open items whose newest kept reply has no keyword go to one `readModel` call, at most `MAX_RULING_ITEMS = 20` per call in index order (the rest stay open this call). A model ruling is accepted only when its disposition is not `none`, its `quote` occurs verbatim (whitespace collapsed) in that reply, its reason is one non-empty line, and a `fixed` ruling's sha occurs in that reply. Otherwise the item stays open and an ask is posted in the thread, unless an own comment with that ask key exists. When `readModel` returns null or throws, no model ruling is accepted and no ask is posted.

For each open item with kept replies, only the newest kept reply is read: `parseRulingKeyword(body)`; a ruling is that item's candidate (`by` = the reply's author). This rule also prevents falling back to an older keyword when the newest reply requires model reading. Every accepted model candidate uses the same echo-before-resolve and checklist path as a keyword candidate; `recordPrRulings` never creates a bot ruling.

Ask key: `wq-<itemKey>-<replyId>`; body `I could not read a ruling from that reply. Start a reply with fixed <sha>, waive: <reason>, confirm, override: <reason> or verified.` Wrap it through the marker helpers and deduplicate only owned asks for that reply. `readModel` returns null or throws — no model rulings; keyword rulings still recorded; no ask. Model ruling fails validation — no ruling; ask posted once per reply.

**Scope** — In: model batch selection, validation, by-attribution, ask posting and tests in rulings-model.test.ts; use US-008's operation-owned types. Out: the prompt/op implementation (US-008), keyword/access and persistence basics (US-009), review/fix wiring (US-011/012). More than 20 model-read items in one call: the rest stay open until the next bot run.

**Interface** — Preserve `recordPrRulings(input)` and `RecordRulingsOutcome`; consume `readModel: (input: BotRulingReadInput) => Promise<BotRulingReadVerdict | null>` and types from `src/operations/bot-ruling-read.ts`. `MAX_RULING_ITEMS = 20`. Model results are candidates attributed to the collaborator, never an authority to waive or override by nax bot.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record PR rulings before trusted workflow review and re-check authorized open finding/ruling item threads alongside earlier bot findings.

**Motivation** — The two review engines drift: `buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt` embeds `WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST` and `WORKFLOW_ENUMERATION_INSTRUCTION` (`src/prompts/builders/workflow-quality-checklist.ts`) and its op retries when `inspectedFiles` misses a changed file (`workflowBranchReviewOp`); `buildBotPrReviewPrompt` has its own six-item `CHECKLIST` with neither, and no coverage retry.

**Approach** — `runBotReview` and `runBotFix`, on a trusted PR whose body has `NAX_WORKFLOW_PR_MARKER`, call `recordPrRulings` after the checkout and before the agent step, with `readModel` calling `botRulingReadOp` with `botModel(config, "rulings")`. A throw is logged and the command continues; its outcome is then absent. This story implements the review half; US-012 implements fix.

`runBotReview` passes the outcome's open items of kind `finding` or `ruling` as `itemEarlier`, resolved or not. `bot-review.json` gains `rulings: { recorded, open, asked }` counts (version stays 2).

Target: also own threads whose opener key starts with `w-`; for those, verdict `fixed` posts a bot ruling echo (`wr-fixed-<itemKey>`, sha = `info.headSha`, the PR head this review read) and resolves the thread, verdict `withdrawn` posts the plain earlier reply and does not resolve, verdict `open` is merged into the agreed items as today with the opener's first line as the issue (the reply instruction is not passed to the fix agent). `withdrawalEvents` stays `f-` only.

`PostReviewInput` (`src/bot/post.ts`). Target: adds optional `itemEarlier?: readonly PrThread[]` (open item threads of kind `finding` or `ruling`), which `postPrReview` treats as part of `earlier` under the rules above; `rulings?: { recorded: number; open: number; asked: number }`, written into `bot-review.json`.

`PrReviewInput.earlier` (`src/bot/review-step.ts`). Target: `runBotReview` passes the own `f-` threads first, then `itemEarlier`; `MAX_EARLIER_THREADS` (50) caps the combined list, and the op's `earlierIds` are the ids of the capped list. Each item thread in it carries only the opener, own comments and the replies whose author has write access (the `kept` replies), so a non-writer cannot steer a bot `fixed` ruling.

**Scope** — In: _botReviewDeps.recordPrRulings seam, raw thread/comment access for recording, filtered combined earlier inputs, post.ts w- fixed/withdrawn/open handling, artifact counts and dedicated integration tests. Out: runBotFix/readyStep (US-012), incremental range (US-013), checklist (US-014), unreadFiles (US-015). A nax bot ruling other than `fixed` is never created by any path. Replies from authors without write access are never rulings, never reopen an item, and are not answered on item threads; on other threads and top-level comments the bot review answers them as today.

userStories.title: Bot fix readies a workflow draft
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace the blanket workflow draft hold with fresh PR ruling checks, exact-head green CI and an idempotent evidence comment.

**Motivation** — `nax bot fix`'s `readyStep` (`src/bot/fix-report.ts`) keeps every nax workflow draft a draft (`WORKFLOW_PR_HOLD`), on purpose until this phase (SPEC-workflow-ci-repair-readiness, Out of Scope).

**Approach** — `runBotReview` and `runBotFix`, on a trusted PR whose body has `NAX_WORKFLOW_PR_MARKER`, call `recordPrRulings` after the checkout and before the agent step, with `readModel` calling `botRulingReadOp` with `botModel(config, "rulings")`. A throw is logged and the command continues; its outcome is then absent. This story implements runBotFix and readyStep; US-011 owns review.

`workflowPrReadiness({ outcome, ci })` returns `{ ready: true }` or `{ ready: false, reason }`, in this order: no outcome (`rulings could not be read`); no index (`no nax item index on this PR`); an index key with no thread (`<n> item(s) without a thread: <ids>`); any open item (`<n> open item(s): <ids>`); CI not `ciAllowsReady` (`CI <outcome>: <detail>`).

`readyStep` on a marked draft: `recordPrRulings` on freshly read threads and comments; the three item checks of `workflowPrReadiness` first, and `waitForChecks` only when they pass; ready: the evidence comment for the settled entries (skipped when there are none), then `markReadyArgv`.

`readyStep` (`src/bot/fix-report.ts`). Baseline: returns `readyHeld: WORKFLOW_PR_HOLD` for a marked PR. Target: a marked PR is decided by `workflowPrReadiness` (below); `WORKFLOW_PR_HOLD` is deleted.

`resolveOwnFindings` (`src/bot/fix-report.ts`). Target: skips agreed items whose key starts with `w-` (nax bot fix never settles an item; the next review does).

`_fixReportDeps` (`src/bot/fix-report.ts`). Target: adds `readPrInfo`, `readCurrentUser`, `listReviewThreads`, `listPrComments` and `recordPrRulings`, which `readyStep` uses to re-read the PR before deciding.

Evidence comment: `evidenceComment(entries)` wrapped with key `w-evidence`; edited in place when it exists. Convert settled rulings to DecisionEntry using sidecarKindFor (ruling -> advisor), preserving a fixed SHA. A retried `readyStep` edits the existing evidence comment; it never posts a second one. If the evidence comment fails, do not mark ready; `readyHeld` = `evidence comment failed: <detail>`. If recording throws, log and hold with `rulings could not be read`. Body ticks do not decide readiness. Bind waitForChecks to the current PR head so pending, failed, unavailable and mismatched-head checks cannot promote.

Workflow PRs published before this change have no index comment, so bot fix holds them with `no nax item index on this PR`; sidecar promote remains available. Removing the workflow marker returns the plain CI-green ready path as before.

The readyStep readModel dispatches botRulingReadOp through callOp with botModel(config, "rulings").

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Review only post-branch-review commits on trusted workflow PRs, or just conversation when the published head is already reviewed.

**Motivation** — `nax bot review` on a nax workflow PR reviews `mergeBase..HEAD` again, although the branch review inside `nax run` already reviewed the branch up to publish.

**Approach** — In `runBotReview`, when the PR is trusted, its body has the workflow marker, the outcome's index names a reviewed head and base, `isAncestor(checkout.worktree, reviewedHead, prHead)` is true, and `isAncestor(checkout.worktree, reviewedBase, mergeBase)` is true (the branch review covered every commit after the merge base):

- PR head equals the reviewed head: `conversationOnly: true`; the prompt says the code at this head was reviewed by the workflow's branch review and findings may come only from what a thread, comment or earlier finding points at, and names no range or package; no package is written; `requiredFiles` is empty.
- otherwise: `rangeBase = reviewedHead`; package and range are `<reviewedHead>..HEAD`.

Any other case, including `Reviewed head: none` and an `isAncestor` throw, keeps today's full review from `mergeBase`.
`requiredFiles` for every non-conversation review is `reviewRequiredFiles` over the package's changed paths. US-015 wires this coverage behavior; this story guarantees the no-package conversation path and range choice it relies on.

`PrReviewInput` (`src/bot/review-step.ts`). Target: adds optional `rangeBase?: string` (default `mergeBase`) and `conversationOnly?: boolean`.
`_botReviewDeps` (`src/bot/review-run.ts`). Target: adds `isAncestor(dir, ancestor, head): Promise<boolean>` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, true on exit 0, false on exit 1, throws otherwise).
`BotPrReviewPromptInput` gains optional `conversationOnly?: boolean`.

Untrusted PRs (fork, author without write access) get no ruling reading and no incremental review; they keep today's static full review. Merging the branch review and the PR review into one engine is not done (user ruling 2026-10-21).

A missing/none/malformed reviewed head or base, either failed ancestry condition, or an ancestry exception must fall back rather than skipping code review. Here prHead means info.headSha and mergeBase means checkout.mergeBase; pass checkout.worktree as the string dir argument, not the PrCheckout object.

Conversation-only does not write even an empty package; non-conversation uses rangeBase for the actual package command as well as the displayed range. Preserve staticMode restrictions and ordinary triage.

userStories.title: Bot review coverage retry
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make bot review retry when required changed files were not inspected and report any files still unread after retry exhaustion.

**Motivation** — The two review engines drift: `buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt` embeds `WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST` and `WORKFLOW_ENUMERATION_INSTRUCTION` (`src/prompts/builders/workflow-quality-checklist.ts`) and its op retries when `inspectedFiles` misses a changed file (`workflowBranchReviewOp`); `buildBotPrReviewPrompt` has its own six-item `CHECKLIST` with neither, and no coverage retry.

**Approach** — `BotPrReviewInput` (`src/operations/bot-pr-review.ts`). Target: adds optional `requiredFiles?: readonly string[]`, `repoRoot?: string`, `range?: string`; when `requiredFiles` is non-empty, the retry `validate` also requires `unreadFiles(requiredFiles, verdict.inspectedFiles, repoRoot)` to be empty, and `invalid` returns `buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(range, missing)` when triage is complete but files are missing.

`PrReviewInput` (`src/bot/review-step.ts`). Target: adds optional `rangeBase?: string` (default `mergeBase`) and `conversationOnly?: boolean`; `runPrReview` passes `requiredFiles` only when non-empty, and its result carries `unreadFiles` = `unreadFiles(requiredFiles, verdict.inspectedFiles, repoRoot)` when non-empty, which `runBotReview` passes to `postPrReview`. The rangeBase/conversation fields arrive from US-013; wire their coverage semantics here.

`PostReviewInput` (`src/bot/post.ts`). Target: adds optional `unreadFiles?: readonly string[]`, rendered by the summary as `Not read by the review: <paths>`.

`requiredFiles` for every non-conversation review is `reviewRequiredFiles` over the package's changed paths. Use the returned changed paths from `writeBranchReviewPackage(projectDir, base, packagePath, opts?)`, and the existing `reviewRequiredFiles(paths, fc)` with config/projectDir/packageDirs from PrStepContext. The existing writePackage wrapper returns void: retain its changed paths for classification while preserving underReviewLimit's package-failure, timeout and abort semantics; do not build the package outside that guarded callback. `repoRoot` is the checkout and `range` is the actual package/prompt range. Conversation-only has no package write and empty requiredFiles; omit requiredFiles on the op when empty.

Match `workflowBranchReviewOp`'s lenient shape parse and exhaustedFallback: coverage influences retry validation, not whether a parseable partial verdict is kept. Missing thread/comment/earlier ids use the triage retry before considering missing-file coverage; only complete triage with missing files gets the coverage retry. `botPrStaticReviewOp` shares validation/retry while retaining its static read-only tool restrictions. Coverage retry still misses files — verdict kept; summary lists the unread files.

**Scope** — In: bot op optional coverage inputs, retry priority/validation, package-path classification in runPrReview, unreadFiles propagation through review graph/posting/summary, and changes to existing op/review-step/summary tests. Out: incremental ancestry/range choice (US-013), shared checklist text (US-014), new reviewer engine. The `.nax/rules/retry-strategy.md` ruled exception must be extended to say the bot review ops' `validate` also requires coverage of the required files; this is a manual edit in the same commit as US-015 (`.nax/` is read-only to the run). Documentation is a manual follow-up after merge.

**Interface** — `BotPrReviewInput` adds `requiredFiles?: readonly string[]`, `repoRoot?: string`, `range?: string`; `PostReviewInput` and the review result carry `unreadFiles?: readonly string[]`. Reuse `unreadFiles` from `src/operations/workflow-review-coverage.ts` and `buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(range, missing)` from @/prompts, not new normalization or retry machinery.

Regression edit: `test/integration/bot/review-step.test.ts` — the assertion that the op input has no `requiredFiles` now expects `requiredFiles` equal to the required changed files of the fixture package (and `repoRoot`, `range`). The invariant: the range and package path arguments are unchanged. Expand existing `test/unit/operations/bot-pr-review.test.ts` and review/summary tests with fake parsed replies and no real agent dispatch.

userStories.title: Promote counts PR rulings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let local workflow promote count current settled PR item rulings alongside local sidecar decisions and report whether PR rulings were readable.

**Motivation** — Those rulings live in a git-ignored sidecar (`src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts`) next to the run, so a fresh checkout (a `nax bot` checkout, a koda job) cannot see them, and nobody can rule from the PR.

**Approach** — `items-ruled` check (`src/cli/workflow-promote.ts`). Target: an open item is ruled when the sidecar has an entry for it or a settled item thread rules it (matched by item key, so the text hash must match the item now); a sidecar entry wins for the same id; the tick and comment actions use the merged entries. `_run:ci` keeps today's rule (it needs a sidecar entry; promote's own CI check is separate). A failure to read the PR threads is logged as a warning and reported in a new report field `prRulings: { read: false, error }` (`{ read: true, count }` otherwise); `checks[].detail` texts are unchanged.

Use `readItemThreads(threads, comments, login)` and `settleItemThreads(read, canRule)`; `canRule(c)` calls `hasWriteAccess(ref, { login: c.author, id: c.authorId }, deps, cwd)` so unauthorized replies after an echo do not unsettle it. Own comments are authored by the current forge login AND carry a valid nax-bot:v1 marker. Only current indexed matching keys can supply PR rulings; do not accept a same-id/different-hash echo. Convert each settled echo to DecisionEntry with its disposition/reason/SHA; the sidecar kind of an item is its `kind`, except `ruling`, which maps to `advisor` (the mapping `sidecarKindFor` applies to an `OpenItem`). Reuse the existing validated sidecar/merge helpers and preserve sidecar precedence for every action, not only the items-ruled check. The report's successful count is the number of settled PR rulings used.

Promote cannot read the PR threads — warning logged, `prRulings.read` false, sidecar entries only. A failure of a reply's access lookup is no access, logged; it must not make a non-writer reply reopen an echoed item. Existing checks[].detail texts, action order, draft checks, CI readiness rule and sidecar validation remain unchanged.

**Scope** — In: workflow-promote.ts PR reads, shared state/access use, current-key ruling merge for items-ruled/tick/evidence and additive prRulings report, helper fixture and existing promote tests. Out: posting or interpreting new rulings (US-005/006/009/010), bot readiness (US-012), changing workflow record. `nax workflow record` stays local; it does not post to the PR. Legacy PRs without an index can still be handled with local sidecar entries; PR-read failure must not block a fully sidecar-ruled promotion.

**Interface** — WorkflowPromoteReport adds `prRulings: { read: false, error }` or `{ read: true, count }`. `readItemThreads` and `settleItemThreads` are the same helpers called by publish/recording; no separate ruling-state algorithm. Keep `_run:ci` sidecar-only and merge by current `itemKey(item)` with sidecar id precedence. Tick/comment consume the merged DecisionEntry list.

Regression edits: `test/helpers/workflow-promote-fixture.ts` — the fake forge answers `api user` with a login and the review-thread and PR-comment reads with empty pages, so promote's new PR reads succeed with no rulings. The invariant: every existing argv answer is unchanged. `test/unit/cli/workflow-promote.test.ts` — expectations on the whole report object gain `prRulings: { read: true, count: 0 }`. The invariant: every `checks[].detail` text and every action is unchanged. Extend existing promote tests for merged entries, sidecar precedence, stale hashes and PR-read failure without moving their behavior to another story.
